title: Minds And Bodies Of His Devotees
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 290
summary: This shabad opens with the minds and bodies of His devotees are infused with His Love. It turns the heart toward o Nanak, He is contained among all.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels unworthy, guarded, and hard-on-self because the shabad keeps mercy inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: O Nanak, He is contained among all.

lines.translation: Love and affection, and the taste of yearning, have welled up within;
within my mind and body, this is my purpose:
beholding with my eyes His Blessed Vision, I am at peace.
My mind blossoms forth in ecstasy, washing the feet of the Holy.

lines.gurmukhi: ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੈ ਮਨਿ ਤਨਿ ਰੰਗੁ ॥
lines.transliteration: bhagat janaa kai man tan ra(n)g ||
lines.translation: The minds and bodies of His devotees are infused with His Love.
Rare is the one who obtains their company.
Show Your mercy - please, grant me this one request:
by Guru's Grace, may I chant the Naam.

lines.gurmukhi: ਤਾ ਕੀ ਉਪਮਾ ਕਹੀ ਨ ਜਾਇ ॥
lines.transliteration: taa kee upamaa kahee na jai ||

lines.translation: O Nanak, He is contained among all. ||6||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: the minds and bodies of His devotees are infused with His Love.
The middle movement widens the correction through rare is the one who obtains their company.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: o Nanak, He is contained among all.
